bifrost: springboard/src/bare/app_policy.rs (launch boundary, no exception mechanism); docs/app-isolation.md
summary: Apple's framework lets a developer tool ask the user for an exception so that locally built software may run under the execution policy (a trust gate on code the developer built). BifrOSt has no such trust gate and no exception mechanism: every installed app launches inside a fail-closed sandbox chosen by the shell, so there is no equivalent to request or record.

features.note: The sandbox decides what an app may touch, not whether a developer tool may be trusted. Nothing asks the user for developer-tool access, and no SDK API exposes it.

The launch boundary is fail-closed with no exception path, as docs/app-isolation.md states (no unrestricted fallback). Adding an exception would weaken that design, so it is intentionally absent rather than missing.

features.feature: Launch enforcement of app policy (the counterpart that gates which code runs)
features.note: Launch is refused when identity, permission validation or sandbox setup fails, and unsupported permissions fail the launch. The system layer enforces this, but apps get no SDK API to query or report the policy error domain.
Launch failures return io errors inside the shell. No typed, app-facing error domain exists for policy failures.

gaps: No app-facing API for developer-tool access requests (EPDeveloperTool); decide with the owner whether a sideload or local-build trust prompt is wanted at all, since the current design has no exception path
Policy launch failures are not exposed to apps as a typed error domain (EPError, EPErrorDomain equivalent)
